Theory.summary: Presenting the main ingredient before the final product increases preference compared to the reverse order, an effect that is stronger when product familiarity is lower.

c1.text: People tend to find it easier to process information when it is presented in a familiar order.

c2.text: The feeling that information processing is easy leads to a sense of familiarity with the subject.

c3.text: An increase in familiarity with the subject increases preference for the subject.

c4.text: Presenting the main ingredient before the final product follows an inherently familiar order based on temporal flow.

c5.text: Consumers' preference for a product is higher when the main ingredient is presented before the product than in the reverse order.

c6.text: The effect of familiar presentation order on preference is greater when product familiarity is lower, and smaller when product familiarity is higher.

c7.text: In the experiment on olive soap, men generally had low familiarity, while women had high familiarity.

h1.text: Men had a significantly higher preference for olive soap when the information was presented in the 'olive oil–olive soap' order compared to the reverse order.

a.note: Men have low product familiarity (c7); finding that they strongly prefer the ingredient-first order confirms Theory's prediction and provides an empirical argument for c5.

h2.text: Women felt information processing was easier in the 'olive soap–olive oil' order than in the reverse order, but men did not feel this way.

b.note: The tempting inference rb1 (that high product familiarity makes product-first order easier, supporting Theory) is undercut by c4: temporal flow (ingredient first) defines the familiar order for all consumers, and familiarity only moderates effect size.

h3.text: Among individuals with similar familiarity with olive soap, there was no significant difference in product preference between men and women.

c.note: Compatible with Theory: the finding that individuals with similar product familiarity have similar preferences does not deny or refute Theory (status of c5 is not OUT).
